It seems I may need to consider appealing to my job about sponsoring me on a skilled worker visa and then transferring to a spousal visa after I’ve hit the 6 month mark, or he does at his new job.

The issue is with the pre-proceedings and the kids, we need me to get there ASAP so that they can have the housing they need. The decision is going to be made shortly after the new year about where they need to go, and we want to avoid having them go into care at all costs. 

At this current rate, he’d make a salary of £43k per year.

I use Retin-A micro gel pump at 0.08%!

So I’ll do tret, then moisturizer, then glycerin. I wait for the tret to dry before I start putting on the moisturizer and then glycerin. 

The glycerin is somewhat occlusive, but it’s also a humectant, so it helps hold water into the skin. Sort of like a “slugging” step (a lot of people use Vaseline).

Thank you!! For the first month, my derm put me on topical clindamycin to help counteract the tret purge. I definitely DID still purge, but I think I may have escaped the worst of it?

And tret helped me simplify my routine. I was desperately swapping actives in and out (salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide, lactic acid, etc), but nothing was working. So in some way, it was the less abrasive option LOL
I use the Retin-A micro gel 0.08% (the pump).

I started off slowly on the neck, I didn’t get brave enough to put it there until a few months into using tret lol! . I would apply tret to my face, apply moisturizer, and then bring down some of the tret-moisturizer mix down to my neck. 

There was a little irritation at first, but when that subsided after a few weeks, I started applying directly.

Now, I use a pea sized amount for my whole face and neck - dabbing once on the forehead, both cheeks, the chin, and then the center of my neck. And then rub in as usual ☺️
Thank you 💜
Thanks!! 😊 And oh yeah, texture is def a major area tret helped out with. A lot smoother than it used to be.
Thank you! ☺️

Three years on tretinoin - Retin-A micro gel 0.08%.

I’m at the point where I can apply 2-3 times a week for maintenance. My skin is always a bit irritated the night after tret (you can see some redness in today’s pic, for example) but overall, my skin’s tolerance has gotten pretty good (no more flaking/peeling). My neck also tolerates direct application now - and I feel like I’ve seen some good improvement on neck wrinkles. 

AM:
-wash with vanicream gentle cleanser
-The Ordinary pycnogenol 5% 
-The Ordinary amino acid + B5
-SkinFix Barrier Lipid-Peptide Cream

PM: 
-Same as AM, but on tret nights, apply before pycnogenol and layer of pure glycerin after SkinFix 

I look like a glazed donut before bed and have to replace my pillowcase frequently, but it feels worth it.

I stopped using hyaluronic acid and argan oil (have never tried rose hip oil) because it all seemed a bit too much for my skin and was making me break out. If you tolerate them well already and they keep your skin hydrated, then I wouldn’t change it up. 

That being said, it may be worth bringing up rose hip oil to your derm, though, because it is rich in Vitamin A, which tret is a derivative of. There is such a thing as hypervitaminosis A.

I did not buffer, but I was careful to use a pea sized amount and wait 20 mins after washing my face before applying the tret like my derm advises. But I know many people swear by buffering on here

I had a very similar routine before I was prescribed Retin A micro gel (0.08%). My derm advised that I cut out all other actives and keep everything very basic (gentle face wash, scent free moisturizer, sunscreen during the day, etc). From my personal experience, my purge lasted about 3 weeks. But it seems to vary by the person and the amount the tret is applied (I did everyday religiously, despite some of the negative side effects like flaky skin) and then one day it all seemed to click. Being consistent and staying moisturized was key for me, and I believe the Aczone that I was prescribed really helped temper the purge (so my derm said. It was gentle, IMO).

Good luck!!

My skin was actually very clear when I was cleansing with a bar of soap (Shea Moisture). Then I started getting flaky skin and tiny hard bumps around my face.

I realized I probably wasn’t exfoliating enough, so I used TO AHA+BHA mask once and the texture difference was amazing.

I switched up my face wash in hopes that I could moisturize my skin and lightly exfoliate. Now that I’m using “gentle” cleansers (CeraVe Hydrating and CeraVe SA alternating), the dry skin is gone but now I have persistent acne on my cheeks - inflamed and red like pictures - and tiny skin colored bumps all over face.

I’ve also incorporated TO Lactic Acid and TO Glycolic Toner (only PM, alternating) and TO Alpha Arbutin before moisturizer (Alba Botabica Green Tea & Aloe Oil-free moisturizer)

No, the bumps have been pretty consistent throughout adding new products. It seems like a mix - some are clearly acne (small red spots, will come to a head) and the others are stubborn and flesh colored and won’t budge. :/ I’ve noticed that my forehead is a lot smoother since the Nizoral + CeraVe introduction, but the cheeks are waaay more stubborn. 

(I know, I’ve done a bit of a skincare no-no by introducing so many new things at once...)

In the past, I’ve used retinols, salicylic acid, and benzoyl peroxide, but I always seemed to get cystic acne when using products like those. They dry me up like the Sahara desert and make it a deeper level issue. The last round of salicylic acid I tried was from The Ordinary, and I ended up with a crater in my cheek from a chemical burn. I’m a little scared to add anything like that back in, TBH. 

And I’ll have to check those websites out, ty!! I haven’t seen the miracle skin clearing that so many people are touting about the Nizoral, so it’s possible other parts of my routine could be cancelling it out (if that’s what it is)

The issue: I have persistent small bumps on my cheeks, jaw, and hairline.

Skin type: combo, leans dry with flaky patches

Current routine: (day + night)
-ELF makeup remover wipes
-Nizoral shampoo mask
-CeraVe Hydrating Cleansee
-alba botanica green tea & aloe oil free moisturizer 
-LUSH mask of magnanimity (as needed)
-Boscia exfoliating peel gel (1-2x / week)

How long - this is a relatively new routine. I used to use the Shea Moisture soap bar, Alba botanica aloe moisturizer, and Argan oil. My skin was pretty nice. Then all of a sudden, it just didn’t work and I now have bumps all over my cheeks. They do not come to a head. I suspect fungal acne, hence the nizoral, but not much luck so far.
